_discipline: All facts here are backed by real Phase 0 spike runs, not model memory. Spike scripts/raw outputs live outside the repo (control_root). Every value cites its evidence.

versions._note: portalocker/pytest-mock were installed during the spike (not pre-installed); mcp SDK is the OFFICIAL 'mcp' package under site-packages, not a local dir. mcp upgraded 1.8.1 -> 1.29.0 and transitive deps refreshed on 2026-08-11 after an OSV security re-scan that returned ZERO advisories for every locked package (all 39) at these versions; the FastMCP stdio contract was re-verified (import path, @mcp.tool() registration, stdio server entry point) in a clean venv, and the full default suite passes (605 at last run; the authoritative count is the live `python -m pytest -q` result).

zcode._summary: How ZCode loads an MCP server and calls a tool — discovered via Task 0.1.

plugin_loaded.evidence: echo MCP server registered in ~/.zcode/cli/config.json -> mcp.servers.echo-spike (stdio). ZCode auto-connects user-scope MCP servers at session start. Verified: the server was connected and its tool was callable from the interactive session.
plugin_loaded._note: Config-file MCP servers do NOT expand ${...} templates — absolute paths required (plugin-provided servers do expand templates).

mcp_stdio.evidence: Official mcp SDK client (stdio_client + ClientSession) drove initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call against echo/server.py directly; all three succeeded.

config_file_mcp.shape: mcp.servers.<name> = { type:'stdio', command:<abs path>, args:[<abs paths>], env:{...}, enabled?, timeoutMs? }
config_file_mcp.template_expansion: NONE for config-file servers; absolute paths required

plugin_manifest.mcpServers_shape: <name>: { command, args[], cwd, env } — plugins DO expand ${ZCODE_PROJECT_DIR}/${ZCODE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/${user_config.KEY}
plugin_manifest.observed_real_example: android-emulator/ios-simulator plugins in the official cache

sdk_import_path.evidence: importlib.util.find_spec('mcp.server.fastmcp') -> FOUND; origin under site-packages, NOT under repo. No local mcp/ shadow (G2 trap avoided).

echo_tool_call.evidence: In a real interactive ZCode session, PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks captured tool_name='mcp__echo-spike__echo' with tool_input={text:'hello'} and toolResponse.content[0].text='{"echo": "hello"}', isError=false.

hooks._summary: Real ZCode hook contract — captured by a temp hook-dumper process hook firing on all 7 events, registered via ~/.zcode/cli/config.json -> hooks (enabled:true). Config-file hooks require hooks.enabled:true.

PermissionRequest._gap: Event existence confirmed by authoritative hook docs + same-source stdin structure as other tool events; real stdin payload NOT captured because ZCode's hook runner runs in the interactive main session while this probe executed in an exec sub-session that has no hook runner. Under yolo/bypass mode the event does not fire at all.

PostToolUseFailure._note: no failing tool call was triggered during the spike; event is supported per docs.

stdin_shape.key_casing: DUAL — every field provided in BOTH snake_case and camelCase (e.g. hook_event_name/hookEventName, tool_name/toolName, tool_input/toolInput, session_id/sessionId, transcript_path/transcriptPath)

hooks.hook_cwd: the project root (e.g. the open repo), NOT the plugin/control root. Plugin root reachable via env var ZCODE_PROJECT_DIR / CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
hooks.feedback_channel: stdout parsed as strict JSON (any extra key fails validation); exit codes as alternative. additionalContext injected into conversation; PreToolUse may return allow/ask/deny; Stop may request continuation.
hooks.stop_reentry_limit: Stop may request continuation up to 3 times (controlled by stopHookActive field).

tool_confirmation._summary: Whether ZCode supports AND how to configure MCP tool-level mandatory human confirmation.
tool_confirmation.mechanism: NOT a per-tool GUI switch. It is permissions.defaultMode + allow/deny rules in ~/.claude/settings.json (Claude-Code-compatible).

yolo.behavior: no confirmation prompts; PermissionRequest hook does NOT fire

confirm_on_change.behavior: prompts before write/side-effecting tool calls; GUI dialog with 3 options

confirmation_dialog.title: 需要权限 / 等待确认
options: 允许 仅允许这一次
始终允许本项目 (后续相同命令不再询问)

tool_confirmation._gap_for_agentflow_v1: MCP-level mandatory confirmation (tool_confirmation gate) is fallback-capable, not required — see gates. The non-adversarial fallback is the convention-based approval flow.

codex._summary: Codex CLI (codex exec) contract for the Planner adapter — confirmed via Task 0.3 on a tiny sample git repo.
codex.auth: Logged in via ChatGPT (~/.codex). A ~/.codex/.env file injects proxy env vars (HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY=<the operator's local proxy>) automatically — codex does NOT need the Adapter to pass proxy explicitly.

stdin_prompt_works.evidence: prompt piped to stdin (`cat prompt.txt | codex exec ...`); codex reads prompt from stdin when no positional PROMPT arg (or `-`) is given. Piped stdin is appended as a <stdin> block when a prompt arg is also present.

read_only_held.evidence: ran with `-s read-only`; after the run the sample repo was clean (git status empty), HEAD unchanged (base==head commit), no tracked/untracked changes. Read-only sandbox held.

cwd_is_repo.evidence: ran with `-C <repo>`; output referenced repo contents (calc.py, README.md). cwd at the repo is how the agent observes files.

output_schema_works.evidence: `--output-schema schema.json` constrained the model's final answer to a JSON object matching the schema; verified the emitted result.json parsed and matched required fields.
output_schema_works.final_message_flag: -o <FILE> / --output-last-message <FILE> — writes the agent's last message to a separate output file (the operation dir, distinct from cwd and prompt)

events_flag.flag: --json — emits JSONL events to stdout (thread.started/turn.started/item.completed/turn.completed); turn.completed carries usage incl. reasoning_output_tokens

reasoning_effort_high_supported.evidence: model_reasoning_effort=high passed with --strict-config returned EXIT=0 (strict-config errors on unrecognized fields/values); an INVALID value ('INSANE') under --strict-config returned EXIT=1. So 'high' is an accepted value, not silently ignored. Default is medium.
reasoning_effort_high_supported._note: reasoning_output_tokens was 0 for the probed model (gpt-5.6-sol) regardless; the config-value acceptance (not token count) is the verified signal.

codex._network_note: Codex core inference works without explicit proxy (ChatGPT login) but emits a benign 'failed to refresh available models: timeout' diagnostic; with the .codex/.env proxy the same warning persists — it is a model-list-refresh subprocess quirk, not a failure of the actual call.
codex._phase4_contract_reminder: prompt (stdin) / cwd (repo) / output dir are THREE distinct concepts; never concatenate prompt into args or let cwd point at control_root.

grok._summary: Grok CLI (grok -p / grok agent) contract for the Reviewer adapter — confirmed via Task 0.4 against a full minimal Review Bundle.

single_turn_flag.flag: -p <PROMPT> / --single <PROMPT> — single-turn, prints response to stdout and exits

readonly_flags.evidence: ran grok -p against the bundle with --permission-mode plan --always-approve; ALL 7 bundle files' SHA256 were byte-identical before vs after the call (no modification), and no new files appeared in the bundle dir.
readonly_flags._critical_cwd_rule: --cwd MUST be an ABSOLUTE Windows path. A relative path => 'Error: 系统找不到指定的文件。 (os error 2)'.
readonly_flags._critical_schema_rule: --json-schema accepts an INLINE JSON string only; '@<file>' syntax is NOT supported ('--json-schema: invalid JSON' error). Pass the schema file contents inline: --json-schema "$(cat schema.json)".

json_output_shape.parsed_result_field: structuredOutput — the already-parsed object matching the schema (authoritative; mirrors the JSON in 'text')

bundle_consumed.evidence: structuredOutput.cited_spec_or_plan quoted SPEC R1/R2 verbatim ('returns a+b for two integers', 'must not change existing behavior') and PLAN Acceptance ('add(2,3)==5'), proving Grok read the SPEC.md/PLAN.md in the bundle.

cwd_vs_bundle_separated.evidence: --cwd points at the bundle dir (the read-only Review Bundle); the model reads bundle files relative to cwd. The call site's actual cwd is irrelevant — Grok uses the --cwd value. cwd (bundle) and prompt (-p arg) are distinct.

network_requires_proxy._critical: Grok has NO automatic proxy injection (unlike codex's ~/.codex/.env). The Adapter MUST explicitly pass HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY=<the operator's proxy> in the subprocess env (sourced from config.yaml reviewer.proxy), otherwise the call HANGS indefinitely (network unreachable). This is a HARD contract for Phase 4 GrokAdapter.

gates._summary: Capability gating (consumed by validate_capabilities in Phase 1). class semantics: required && value==false => startup fail; optional => never blocks; fallback-capable && value==false => allowed only if its fallback is acceptable per config; unknown => block.

planner_ok.evidence: codex.stdin_prompt_works + read_only_held + cwd_is_repo + output_schema_works all true (Task 0.3).

reviewer_ok.evidence: grok.readonly_flags + bundle_consumed + json_output_shape + cwd_vs_bundle_separated all true (Task 0.4).

tool_confirmation.evidence: zcode.tool_confirmation.supported=true. Whether it is configured depends on the operator's ~/.claude/settings.json (permissions.defaultMode). The Phase-0 spike env ran defaultMode=yolo/bypassPermissions, so MCP-level mandatory confirmation was NOT enforced there; other environments may differ. The fallback is the convention-based approval flow (workflow_approve_spec gate node).

reasoning_effort_high.evidence: codex.reasoning_effort_high_supported=true (--strict-config accepted 'high'). Fallback medium is the codex default and always available.
reasoning_effort_high._note: Even though high works, the gate stays fallback-capable so a future model/account without high can degrade to medium rather than block startup.

mcp_stdio_server.evidence: zcode.mcp_stdio + plugin_loaded + echo_tool_call all true (Task 0.1). The AgentFlow server is itself a FastMCP stdio server loaded the same way.

hook_contract_known.evidence: zcode.hooks: 6/7 events real-captured + full stdin dual-key structure + exit codes + cwd. PermissionRequest event confirmed (payload gap documented, does not block).
hook_contract_known._note: Required for Phase 7 (gate_on_stop / protect_artifacts hooks). No unknown remains that would block hook implementation.

network_isolation.note: v1 advisory-only; true OS-level network isolation is out of scope. codex/grok run with proxy to reach model APIs; the sandbox flags (-s read-only / --permission-mode plan) provide FILESYSTEM read-only, not network isolation.
network_isolation._note: Threat model (Spec): MCP provides process-integrity, not defense against same-privilege malicious processes.

proxy_required_for_external_llm.evidence: grok hangs without explicit proxy env (HTTP(S)_PROXY=<operator proxy>); codex injects its own via ~/.codex/.env. The Phase 4 adapters MUST pass proxy env to grok subprocess (sourced from config); codex works either way.
proxy_required_for_external_llm._note: This is an environment finding, not a product feature. Documented so the Adapter does not assume env inheritance.
